subject: Rebaseline request: MAP dates + action cascade (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Tim Rogers <tim@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Need to shift MAP + target close (quick heads-up)

Jordan —

Quick note from our side: Procurement just flagged a dependency on a security attestation that will likely push our internal acceptance window by 10 business days. The technical reviews (security & legal) are still positive overall, but they want the SOC2 addendum to be signed before final acceptance.

We want to avoid derailing the whole go-live, so can you and your team propose a short rebaseline for the MAP that preserves the canary/acceptance gates but shifts the final sign-off by ~2 weeks?

Also, curious whether Redwood can accommodate a temporary SLA concession for the canary period (lower penalties, more flexible cutover) while procurement completes the paperwork. If there’s a playbook for this (credits or short-term SLA exceptions) that would help smooth internal approvals.

Appreciate a quick plan — we’re hoping to still hit an early July production ramp if possible.

Thanks,
Tim Rogers
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Health

-----

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Rogers <tim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need to shift MAP + target close (quick heads-up)

Tim — thanks for the heads-up. Sorry to hear procurement needs the attestation in place — that’s a common friction point.

Short answer: yes, we can rebaseline and propose an action cascade that keeps a canary/limited go-live earlier while the final acceptance slips. Below is a concrete proposal we can iterate on:

- Proposed rebaseline: shift Final Sign-off from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-14 (10 business days).
- Canary/limited production: keep the canary start at 2026-07-01 (rollout to a small segment) conditional on completion of the security attestation review (we can accept a signed attestation by 2026-07-07 to proceed).
- Acceptance gates: preserve the evaluation checklist for performance, reliability, and data handling. If any key metric fails, we stop the canary and default to the original cadence.
- SLA exception: Naomi (cc’d) — can you summarize the standard SLA concession options we offer for cases like this and confirm whether finance needs an approval path for any credit issuance?
- Action owners: Camila (technical), Naomi (commercial/finance), Jordan (project owner / exec sponsor).

I’ll attach a draft MAP rebaseline and a short escalation note we can share with your procurement team. If you can confirm by EOD tomorrow, we’ll circulate the revised MAP and an exec sign-off template.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Rebaseline_MAP_v2.xlsx (draft)

-----

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Tim Rogers <tim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need to shift MAP + target close (quick heads-up)

Hi all — quick technical note from our side about risk/mitigation for the canary plan.

1) Attestation timeline: if procurement needs a signed attestation doc before acceptance, we can provisionally proceed with canary (limited to non-sensitive datasets) because the canary tests do not require full PHI ingest. We need the attestation signed before expanding to full dataset.

2) Cutover rollback: we’ll include an automated rollback window (48 hours) and a hotfix playbook for tokenization issues. Camila will own the rollback readiness checklist and runbook.

3) Monitoring thresholds: suggested thresholds for canary: 95th percentile latency < 400ms, error rate < 0.5% sustained over 30m, and embedding coverage >= 98%. If any threshold is breached we pause and revert.

I’ve updated the attached MAP draft to call out the dataset restriction for the canary and added the rollback checklist (tab 3).

Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Rebaseline_MAP_v2.xlsx (updated)

-----

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Tim Rogers <tim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need to shift MAP + target close (quick heads-up)

Tim / Jordan —

Thanks — we reviewed the rebaseline draft and the canary guardrails. Commercial update: finance can approve a one-time credit against the July invoice to reduce procurement friction, but we require a brief SLA exception request submitted via our internal approval form. I’ve attached the SLA_exception_request.pdf and filled in the commercial rationale.

What I’m proposing:
- Redwood issues a $15k credit to be applied to the July invoice contingent on the attestation being delivered by 2026-07-07.
- We’ll provide an interim SLA exception for the canary period (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-14) that reduces penalty exposure and changes escalation contacts to the on-call team.

Next steps I need from Acme:
1) Procurement to confirm the attestation timeline and send the draft attestation to legal@redwood.ai for a quick review.
2) Confirm acceptance of the limited-data canary scope (Camila’s note).
3) Tim to confirm whether Acme accepts the credit & SLA exception approach so we can route approvals.

Jordan — once Tim confirms I’ll start the approval flow and attach the finalized credit note to the MAP.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_exception_request.pdf

-----

From: Tim Rogers <tim@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need to shift MAP + target close (quick heads-up)

Jordan / Naomi / Camila —

Thanks — confirming: procurement can aim to get the signed attestation to you by 2026-07-06 (one day earlier than your contingency). Acme accepts the limited-data canary scope and the credit & SLA exception approach looks reasonable to our procurement/legal teams.

We’ll send the draft attestation to legal@redwood.ai by Friday (2026-06-20). Marking the new Final Sign-off target as 2026-07-14 and Canary start 2026-07-01 on our calendar.

Tim
